'''''Narcissus cavanillesii''''' is a species of ''[[Narcissus (plant)|Narcissus]]'' (daffodils) in the family [[Amaryllidaceae]] native to the [[Iberian Peninsula]] and [[Northwest Africa]]. It is classified in [[Section (botany)|section]] ''Tapeinanthus'', of which it is the sole member. Formerly, it was classified as a separate genus, ''Tapeinanthus''.

==Description==
''Narcissus cavanillesii'' is a [[bulbous]] plant, {{convert|8|-|18|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall.<ref>{{cite web |title=Narcissus cavanillesii |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/20_184_05_Narcissus.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=26 December 2020}}</ref> Unlike the remaining species of ''Narcissus'', the [[Perianth#Corona|corona]] is almost completely absent, which was why it was formerly classified as a separate genus.

==Distribution and habitat==
''Narcissus cavanillesii'' is native to the southwest [[Iberian Peninsula]] and [[Northwest Africa]] (in Morocco, south to [[Agadir]], and Algeria) and inhabits forest clearings, scrublands, Mediterranean pastures, riparian communities and road edges in sub-humid Mediterranean climates from sea level up to {{convert|730|m|ft|abbr=on}} [[Height above sea level|a.s.l.]], occasionally {{convert|1000|m|ft|abbr=on}}.<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" />
